reading.title: A Busy Morning
reading.text: This morning I got up at 6.30 because my bus leaves early. I turned on the light, took off my pyjamas and put on my school clothes. My mother turned on the TV to watch the news, but my father said, "Turn it down, please." Then I ran to the bus stop. The bus was already there, so I got on. When we arrived at school, I got off and went to the classroom. The teacher said, "Come on, we are late!" She turned off the lights and we went to the gym. Today we play basketball.

reading.title: Dilshod's Day
reading.text: Dilshod wakes up at seven o'clock every morning. He gets up, has a shower and has breakfast. He listens to the radio while he eats. At half past eight he goes to work by bus. He comes home at six. His wife makes dinner and they watch TV. Sometimes Dilshod phones a friend or writes emails. On Saturday he washes clothes and cleans the house. Three times a week he goes for a walk in the park. He goes to bed at eleven o'clock. He says that his days are simple but happy.

reading.title: A Phone Call with Grandma
reading.text: Yesterday my grandmother phoned me. She said, "Hello, how are you?" I told her that I was fine. She asked me what I was doing. I said, "I am doing my homework." She told me a funny story about her neighbour, and we both laughed. Then she asked me to tell her about my new school. I told her about my teacher and my friends. Grandma speaks three languages, so she asked me if I like English. I said yes, and I said a few words in English. She replied, "Very good!" Before she said goodbye, she told me she would visit us on Sunday.

reading.title: Sports Day
reading.text: Last Friday was Sports Day at our school. Early in the morning we walked to the stadium. The teacher said, "First, run around the track!" We ran very fast. Then we jumped over a small wall. Some students climbed a rope. Bobur fell and hurt his knee, but he got up and continued. In the afternoon we went swimming in the pool. After that we danced to music. At the end, we rode our bikes home. My father came to the school by car, but he drove very slowly because there were many students. It was a tiring but wonderful day.

reading.title: Why I Like My Town
reading.text: I like my town because it is small and quiet. It is smaller than the capital, but it is also more beautiful. You can walk to school, or you can take a bus. In summer we swim in the river and have picnics. We go home before it gets dark. If it rains, we stay at home and play games. My brother likes the town too, but he wants to live in the city when he is older. I say, "You can go to the city, but you will miss the quiet." Maybe he is right, so we will see.
